title: Impact of Mental Health-related Condition on Eligibility for Home Protection Scheme
what_it_is: Impact of Mental Health-related Condition on Eligibility for Home Protection Scheme

sections.label: Mental health and HPS eligibility
sections.summary: HPS eligibility is assessed on severity, prognosis, control and health risk profile, not mental health condition alone, though serious pre-existing conditions are excluded.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Having a mental health-related condition is not necessarily a ground that would make a person ineligible for the HPS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Instead, a member's eligibility for the HPS is assessed based on the overall severity, prognosis and control of the medical condition as well as their health risk profile.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Hence, even for members with pre-existing mental health-related conditions, a majority of them are covered under the scheme because their conditions are assessed by medical professionals to be mild or moderate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, the HPS coverage is not extended to applicants with serious pre-existing medical conditions, including serious mental health-related conditions, if they are assessed to have significantly higher risk of mortality.

sections.label: Data review and HPS sustainability
sections.summary: The Government relies on medical experts, requires upfront disclosure of pre-existing conditions, reviews data continuously, and keeps HPS sustainable and affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My second supplementary question is, when looking at these issues, does the Government take into consideration that whatever the actuarial science says about people with mental health conditions who go on to schemes like this, that data may have come about in the past when the extent of diagnosis of mental health conditions was maybe much, much less than what it is now and what it will be in the future, with growing awareness of mental health issues, and as we move away from the stigmatisation and discrimination of people with mental health conditions, and you can expect that more people will be diagnosed – so, are we using data from the past in order to draw an actuarial conclusion about the present day?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We do take a nuanced approach; we depend on medical experts; we are certainly not the experts in determining what is the level of severity, the prognosis, to whether the actuarial risks associated with the mortality or morbidity, as a result of a particular illness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: What we do need, however, is for the members, at the point of signing, to disclose upfront the pre-existing conditions that they have.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To the second supplementary question, in terms of the extent of the diagnosis, we constantly and continuously review the data that is available.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And I think this is not something that is carved in stone in terms of the coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: However, because of the fact that the HPS is constructed to be as widespread and as pervasive as possible to support the broadest segment of our population in their home protection – for them to be able to continue to cover the loans in the event of total permanent disability and so on and so forth – we also want to keep the scheme sustainable and affordable.
